answer: A reward pool treats keys with identical 100-bit error vectors as one claimant. Each key answers 40 fable-inference tests, 30 plume-source image matches and 30 onyx-spectrum matches; a bit marks disagreement with a committed reference answer. After submissions close, a verifier reveals cases, recomputes vectors and divides 1 reward among keys sharing a vector. Exact clones cannot grow their group's payout by splitting keys. Diverse errors evade grouping, and equally accurate honest agents can be merged.
